entries.test: Public records of OpenAI’s strategy and resource commitments, together with results from scaling its models, would show whether the company depended on scaling and whether that strategy had delivered the promised general intelligence.
entries.note: “Bet the entire company” has a plain reading as strategic dependence. Failure to deliver AGI so far would not establish that scaling can never deliver it.

entries.test: Published historical accounts would show whether historians write about US damage from reliance on scaling, the Trump administration’s embrace of it, and losses of state autonomy.
entries.note: The plain reading predicts historical writing on these themes. Economic collapse is explicitly only a possibility.

The examples defining “like these” are absent, so the added thematic description cannot be verified as faithful. “I anticipate” expresses a firm expectation; the missing referent prevents a shared test.
Marcus explicitly re-endorses his own earlier passage. Its main commitment is that scaling’s limitations should give us pause.
“Likely” explicitly qualifies the forecast. “Half the battle” is figurative rather than a numerical threshold.

entries.test: Public documentation of a demonstrated AGI’s development would show whether it incorporated lessons from human reasoning, physical understanding, language, and concept learning.
entries.note: This asserts a necessary condition for building AGI. A demonstrated AGI developed without those lessons would falsify it.
